seo.description: Visit the Sea Castle (Qasr al-Bahr) in Safi: 16th-century Portuguese fortress above the Atlantic, best light and practical tips.
seo.og_title: Sea Castle, Safi: Portuguese Fortress on the Atlantic
seo.og_description: How to visit Safi’s sea fortress: walls above the ocean and evening light.

name: Castillo del Mar
hero_subtitle: 16th-century Portuguese fortress rising above the Atlantic.

overview.title: A fortress on the waves
overview.p1: The Sea Castle, or Qasr al-Bahr, is a Portuguese fortress built in the 16th century to control Safi’s harbour. Its walls rise directly above the Atlantic.
overview.p2: It is one of the city’s most photographed landmarks. Evening light brings out the stone and the open ocean.
overview.p3: Combine it with a walk through the medina and the fishing port for a full half-day by the sea.

moods.subtitle: When to go for the best light and calm.

1.title: Quiet visit
1.desc: Fewer people and softer light on the stone.

2.title: Strong light
2.desc: Harsh sun; better for a short stop if you are nearby.

3.title: Best colour
3.desc: Warm light on stone and ocean — the classic photo window.

food.title: Food near the Sea Castle
food.p1: Restaurants are mainly around the port and the waterfront.
food.li1: Fish restaurants at the fishing port.
food.li5: Bring water before or after the visit.
food.p2: Cash is useful for small places.

tips.title: Practical tips for the Sea Castle

1.title: Watch your footing
1.desc: Ramparts and edges can be uneven. Stay on clear paths, especially with children or in wind.

2.title: Golden hour
2.desc: Aim for late afternoon if you want the best photos of the walls against the Atlantic.

3.title: Combine stops
3.desc: Pair with the medina or the fishing port so the visit is part of a wider walk.

q1.question: How much time for the Sea Castle?
q1.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is usually enough for the walls, views and photos.

q2.question: Is there an entry fee?
q2.answer: Many outdoor areas are free; check on site if any section is ticketed.

q3.question: Can I visit with children?
q3.answer: Yes, with supervision near edges and uneven ground.

q4.question: Is it open every day?
q4.answer: Outdoor ramparts are generally accessible daily.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required. A local guide adds history; the fortress is readable on its own.
